statement: Every acceptance criterion in the task's triage_note is met on the run's own branch: by tested code that follows specs which agree with each other, or by those specs alone in a docs-only run.

deliverables.where: the task's triage note, in the run's branch

judge.stance: The task's acceptance criteria and the files on the run's branch are the truth; everything a step said is a claim to verify. Judge meaning, not wording.

final.text: Every file the run changed is committed on the run's own branch
final.check_method: Read the git facts of the worktree: no uncommitted change, no untracked file outside the ignore rules

final.text: Every spec the run edited passes the spec rule's structure check
final.check_method: For each edited `*.spec.md`: a Purpose section, at least one behaviour in the fixed pattern with a scenario, at least one acceptance criterion, each behaviour named by a criterion, each criterion naming a behaviour

final.text: No spec the run edited is over 400 lines
final.check_method: Count the lines of each edited `*.spec.md`

final.text: Every id that a spec the run edited links to resolves to exactly one definition
final.check_method: Collect the ids each edited spec links; search the docs folders for each id's definition; fail on none or on more than one

final.text: Every acceptance criterion of each spec the run edited is named by at least one test
final.check_method: Search the test folders for each criterion id; N/A when the run delivers documents only

final.text: Every verification command the plan lists exits 0 on the branch head
final.check_method: Run each command through the engine's command runner, reusing the code gate's run on an unchanged tree; N/A when the run delivers documents only

final.text: No spec file is edited without a change to a behaviour or an acceptance criterion
final.check_method: Diff each edited spec against the run's base commit; report each file whose diff touches no behaviour block and no criterion row

final.text: No behaviour in a spec the run edited contradicts a behaviour in a spec it links to
final.check_method: Read each edited spec, then each spec it links by id; compare the behaviours that share a subject

scale.met: every pair of behaviours that share a subject states compatible results
scale.partial: one pair differs only in wording that a reader could take two ways
scale.unmet: two behaviours state results that cannot both hold
scale.evidence: the ids of the behaviours compared, with a quote of each

final.text: Each acceptance criterion of the task is achieved by the run's commits
final.check_method: Take the numbered acceptance criteria from the triage note; for each, find the commit content that achieves it

scale.met: each criterion is achieved, by code with a passing test or by a document when the run delivers documents only
scale.partial: each criterion is addressed but one is achieved only in part
scale.unmet: one criterion has nothing in the commits that achieves it
scale.evidence: per criterion number: the path and line that achieve it

triage.statement: The triage note states the task's acceptance criteria, the gaps in the specs, and a route that follows the gaps

criteria.text: The triage note has each section the triage rule requires
criteria.check_method: Read the note's headings against the rule's list

criteria.text: The route value is `plan` exactly when the gap list is `none`
criteria.check_method: Compare the two values the step handed over

criteria.text: Every file the triage step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every acceptance criterion in the triage note is stated by the task
criteria.check_method: Read the task, then each numbered criterion of the note

scale.met: each criterion is a statement the task makes, with none added and none missing
scale.partial: each criterion comes from the task but one is reworded so that its meaning shifts
scale.unmet: a criterion is in the note that the task does not state, or one the task states is missing
scale.evidence: per criterion: the quote from the task

criteria.text: Every concept the task needs that no ready spec covers is listed as a gap
criteria.check_method: Search the spec folders for each concept the task names; compare with the gap list

scale.met: each concept without a ready spec is a gap row, each gap row names the search that found nothing
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a concept has no ready spec yet no gap row lists it
scale.evidence: per concept: the spec path that covers it, or the search that found none

discovery.statement: Every gap is closed by a spec, a decision record or a research note in the agreed format, committed

criteria.text: Every spec the discovery step wrote passes the spec rule's structure check
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-form, on the files this step changed

criteria.text: Every document the discovery step created carries its type suffix in its file name
criteria.check_method: Match each new file under the docs folders against the naming table

criteria.text: Every id that a document of the discovery step links to resolves to exactly one definition
criteria.check_method: As ts-spec-links, on the files this step changed

criteria.text: Every file the discovery step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every gap in the triage note is closed by a document the hand-off names
criteria.check_method: Read the gap rows, then the document the hand-off names for each

scale.met: each gap row has a document whose content settles the gap
scale.partial: each gap has a document but one leaves an open question that blocks planning
scale.unmet: a gap row has no document, or its document does not address the gap
scale.evidence: per gap: the path and the behaviour id or section that settles it

criteria.text: Every behaviour the discovery step wrote states an observable result with no internal name
criteria.check_method: Read each new or changed behaviour; a name is allowed only when someone outside the capability depends on it

scale.met: each behaviour names an event and a result an outside observer could see, with no class, function or module name
scale.partial: each behaviour is observable but one carries an internal name that could be removed without loss
scale.unmet: a behaviour describes how the code works, not what an observer sees
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the quoted sentence

criteria.text: No document the discovery step wrote covers a concept outside the task's gaps
criteria.check_method: Compare each changed document with the gap rows

scale.met: each changed document maps to a gap row
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a document adds behaviour no gap row asks for
scale.evidence: per document: the gap row it serves

plan.statement: The plan traces every acceptance criterion to requirements and phases, states its complexity, and agrees with the specs

criteria.text: The plan has each section the plan rule requires
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's headings and its hand-off section against the rule's list

criteria.text: Every acceptance criterion in the triage note is named by at least one plan requirement
criteria.check_method: Match criterion numbers between the note and the plan's requirement table

criteria.text: The complexity value matches the plan's measured signs
criteria.check_method: Count phases, task rows, test rows, files, commands and reading-set bytes, and read each phase's weight; compare with the rule's limits for `simple`

criteria.text: Every file the plan step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: No plan requirement contradicts a behaviour of a spec the plan references
criteria.check_method: Read each requirement, then the behaviours of each spec the plan references

scale.met: each requirement follows from a behaviour or an acceptance criterion
scale.partial: each requirement is compatible but one goes beyond what any behaviour states
scale.unmet: a requirement states a result a referenced behaviour forbids
scale.evidence: per requirement id: the behaviour id it follows from

expand.statement: Every phase of a complex plan has task rows with tests first and verification commands that run

criteria.text: Every phase of the plan has at least one task row
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's phase headings and task tables

criteria.text: Every code row is preceded by a test row that names an acceptance criterion id
criteria.check_method: Read the row order of each task table

criteria.text: Every verification command in the plan resolves against the repository's allowed commands
criteria.check_method: Resolve each command with the engine's command resolver, without running it

criteria.text: Every file the expand step changed is committed
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: Every task row implements a requirement of the plan with no change to the plan's design
criteria.check_method: Read the design sections as approved at the plan gate, then each task row

scale.met: each row names the requirement it implements, with the design sections unchanged
scale.partial: each row implements a requirement but one row's file or scope is too loose to act on
scale.unmet: a row implements nothing in the design, or the design sections were rewritten
scale.evidence: per row id: the requirement id

code.statement: The whole plan is built test first, committed, with the plan's verification passing in the gate's own run

criteria.text: Every task row of the plan is marked done
criteria.check_method: Read the plan's task rows, then the row table of the code report

criteria.text: Every verification command the plan lists exits 0 when the gate runs it
criteria.check_method: Run each command through the engine's command runner with the test budget

criteria.text: Every file the code step changed is committed with no commit on a remote
criteria.check_method: Read the git facts

criteria.text: The code change agrees by meaning with every behaviour of each spec the run edited
criteria.check_method: Read the changed paths and the edited specs the check lists. For each behaviour of each edited spec, read its scenarios, then the code that implements it. Judge the meaning, not the wording or the names

scale.met: each behaviour's scenarios hold in the code as written, with nothing in the diff that a behaviour forbids
scale.partial: each behaviour holds in its main scenario but one further scenario is not handled by the code
scale.unmet: the code does something a behaviour forbids, or a behaviour of an edited spec has no code
scale.evidence: per behaviour id: the file and line of the code that implements it

criteria.text: The code change breaks no behaviour of a related spec that the run did not edit
criteria.check_method: Related specs are those an edited spec links by id plus those the plan references; the check lists them. Read their behaviours against the changed code

scale.met: no behaviour of a related spec is contradicted by the diff
scale.partial: no contradiction, but one related behaviour now depends on code the diff changed with no test that covers it
scale.unmet: the diff makes a behaviour of a related spec false
scale.evidence: per related spec: the behaviour ids read, with the diff lines compared

criteria.text: Each task row's change is in the file the row names
criteria.check_method: Read each row, then the file it names

scale.met: each row's change is present in its named file
scale.partial: each row's change exists but one sits in a different file than the row names
scale.unmet: a row is marked done with no matching change
scale.evidence: per row id: the path and line

criteria.text: Each test that carries an acceptance criterion id asserts what that criterion states
criteria.check_method: Read each test that names a criterion id, then the criterion in its spec

scale.met: each such test fails if the criterion's result is absent
scale.partial: each test exercises the behaviour but one asserts a weaker result than the criterion
scale.unmet: a test carries a criterion id yet asserts nothing about it, or is skipped
scale.evidence: per criterion id: the test name and the asserting line

criteria.text: No file is changed that no task row names
criteria.check_method: Compare the changed paths with the files the rows name

scale.met: each changed path is named by a row
scale.partial: no partial: any gap is UNMET
scale.unmet: a changed path has no row
scale.evidence: the changed paths with their row ids

assumptions: Per-phase coding waits for the engine's sequential map; until then a complex plan is coded in one session.

The plan, the code report and the discovery hand-off are not listed as deliverables because the engine requires every listed deliverable on every path, and a docs-only run or a run with no gaps does not produce them all.
No step or judge uses the large model tier.
Whether the code agrees with the specs by meaning is judged once, at the code gate (ts-code-aligned, ts-code-related), not again at the outcome gate.
The release step and a work-tracker start are left out of the first version.

Verification commands resolve against one fixed list (pytest, ruff, mypy and read-only git) because release 1 of the engine reads no per-repository command resolver; a repository with another toolchain adds its prefixes to the workflow's list.
Whether a commit is absent from every remote is not checked: the engine's git facts do not report it in release 1. Steps cannot push, and only the last stage does.
